```{r setup, include=FALSE}
                      fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5)

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(knitr)
library(zoo)

library(whychusModel)
library(randomForest)

```

# Objective

`rm85-rf-dynamical.Rmd` trains a random forest to predict RM 8.5's 7DADM
directly. Against the real 2026 NWS hindcast that model carries a cold bias
that grows with lead and concentrates in exactly the conditions the HCP
threshold cares about — reaching -1.85°C on days observed at or above 20°C
at lead 7, where it barely outperforms simply carrying today's value
forward (RMSE 2.01 vs. persistence's 2.05).

Diagnosis (worked through in detail before this document was written):

* **Not** a warm-tail extrapolation problem. 31% of training rows are
  already ≥20°C and the training maximum (24.06°C) exceeds anything
  observed in 2026 (23.1°C); the prediction ceiling gap is under 0.9°C.
* It is a **train/serve mismatch**. The model trains on archived GFS
  weather but is served real NWS forecasts, and those two disagree by
  1.7°C MAE at lead 1 growing to 2.8°C at lead 7 (cloud cover is worse
  still: +15 pp bias, r falling to 0.58). A model that predicts an
  absolute temperature leans hard on those mismatched weather columns, so
  it degrades badly at long leads in the real world.

This document reframes the target as the **change from today** rather than
the absolute level: the forest is trained on `rm_8_5_7dadm - dadm_m0` and
the prediction adds `dadm_m0` back. Because `dadm_m0` is a real RM 8.5
observation — identical at training and serving time — the model is
anchored on something the mismatch cannot corrupt, and only has to learn
the correction. Measured on the real 2026 hindcast, that single change is
worth -0.29 to -0.40 RMSE (paired t-test, p < 0.001), roughly 6-10x larger
than any effect from swapping the weather source itself.

Two supporting additions, each independently significant (p < 0.001):

* **RM 8.5's own trend** (`dadm_trend`, `tmax_trend`) — the model
  previously had trend features for Camp Polk but none for RM 8.5 itself.
* **Trajectory summaries** (`traj_air_max_max`, `traj_air_max_mean`,
  `traj_air_min_mean`, `traj_warming`) — at lead 7 the forecast spans 28
  individual columns and `mtry` samples only a third of them, so explicit
  summaries concentrate a signal the forest otherwise has to rediscover.

Everything else is unchanged from `rm85-rf-dynamical.Rmd`: same
dynamical.org GFS weather source, same 500-tree forests, same
chronological 80/20 split, same same-day RM 8.5 inputs. A head-to-head
against Open-Meteo's Previous Runs archive found no significant difference
in skill at this configuration (p = 0.46), so the source is left as-is.

```{r config}
month_start     <- 5
month_end       <- 10
lead_days_vec   <- c(1:7)
ntree           <- 500
test_frac       <- 0.20
trend_window    <- 5
threshold_7dadm <- 20.0

# Most recent RM 8.5 logger export. Kept as a config value because the
# hindcast window is bounded by it — point this at the newest export and
# keep it in step with summer_2026_8_5_performance.Rmd.
rm85_logger_file <- "WC85 Rimrock bottom 2026-08-13 09_52_44 PDT.xlsx"

lead_colors <- setNames(colorRampPalette(c("#185FA5", "#4E9F50", "#C93312"))(length(lead_days_vec)),
                        as.character(lead_days_vec))
```

# Data & feature construction

```{r load-data}
rm85_7dadm <- rm_8_5_historical |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) |>
  filter(statistic == "7DADM") |>
  select(date, rm_8_5_7dadm = temperature)

rm85_tmax <- rm_8_5_historical |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) |>
  filter(statistic == "max") |>
  select(date, rm_8_5_tmax = temperature)

cp_7dadm <- camp_polk_temperature_historical |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) |>
  filter(statistic == "7DADM") |>
  select(date, cp_7dadm = temperature)

cp_tmax <- camp_polk_temperature_historical |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) |>
  filter(statistic == "max") |>
  select(date, cp_tmax = temperature)

cp_flow <- camp_polk_flow_historical |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) |>
  filter(statistic == "mean") |>
  select(date, cp_flow_mean = flow_cfs)

dyn_raw <- read_csv(here("data-raw", "dynamical_gfs_air_temp_historical.csv")) |>
  mutate(valid_date = as.Date(valid_date))

cat(sprintf("dynamical.org archive: %s to %s, %d rows\n",
            min(dyn_raw$valid_date), max(dyn_raw$valid_date), nrow(dyn_raw)))
```

```{r helpers}
get_forecast_dyn <- function(lead_k) {
  dyn_raw |>
    filter(lead_days == lead_k) |>
    select(valid_date, variable, value) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = value) |>
    rename(date = valid_date, air_max = temperature_2m_max,
           air_min = temperature_2m_min, cloud_pct = cloud_cover_mean)
}

get_forecast_trajectory_dyn <- function(lead_k) {
  day_tables <- map(seq_len(lead_k), function(k) {
    get_forecast_dyn(k) |>
      mutate(run_date = date - k) |>
      transmute(
        run_date,
        !!paste0("air_max_d", k) := air_max,
        !!paste0("air_min_d", k) := air_min,
        !!paste0("cloud_d",   k) := cloud_pct,
        !!paste0("julian_d",  k) := yday(date)
      )
  })
  reduce(day_tables, full_join, by = "run_date") |> arrange(run_date)
}

# Collapses the d1..dk trajectory into a handful of explicit summaries. At
# lead 7 the raw trajectory is 28 columns and mtry samples ~9 of them, so a
# tree often misses the days that actually matter; these give it the shape
# of the week directly. `traj_warming` (last day minus first) is the
# ramping-up signal that a persistence-anchored model needs in order to
# break away from today's value during a developing hot spell.
add_trajectory_summaries <- function(df, lead_k) {
  air_max_cols <- as.matrix(df[, paste0("air_max_d", 1:lead_k), drop = FALSE])
  air_min_cols <- as.matrix(df[, paste0("air_min_d", 1:lead_k), drop = FALSE])
  df$traj_air_max_max  <- apply(air_max_cols, 1, max)
  df$traj_air_max_mean <- apply(air_max_cols, 1, mean)
  df$traj_air_min_mean <- apply(air_min_cols, 1, mean)
  df$traj_warming      <- air_max_cols[, lead_k] - air_max_cols[, 1]
  df
}

build_df_dyn <- function(lead_k) {
  fcst_traj <- get_forecast_trajectory_dyn(lead_k) |>
    mutate(date = run_date + lead_k) |>
    select(-run_date)

  joined <- rm85_7dadm |>
    left_join(cp_flow  |> mutate(date = date + lead_k), by = "date") |>
    left_join(cp_7dadm |> mutate(date = date + lead_k), by = "date") |>
    left_join(cp_tmax  |> mutate(date = date + lead_k), by = "date") |>
    left_join(fcst_traj, by = "date") |>
    left_join(cp_flow  |> mutate(date = date + lead_k + 1)            |> rename(cp_flow_m1  = cp_flow_mean), by = "date") |>
    left_join(cp_flow  |> mutate(date = date + lead_k + trend_window) |> rename(cp_flow_mw  = cp_flow_mean), by = "date") |>
    left_join(cp_7dadm |> mutate(date = date + lead_k + 1)            |> rename(cp_7dadm_m1 = cp_7dadm),     by = "date") |>
    left_join(cp_7dadm |> mutate(date = date + lead_k + trend_window) |> rename(cp_7dadm_mw = cp_7dadm),     by = "date") |>
    # RM 8.5's own same-day values — no lag. The operational script runs at
    # 7pm PST and RM 8.5's daily max lands by 5-6pm on essentially every day
    # in the real 2026 record (0% after 7pm, 4.1% after 6pm), so today's
    # reading is complete at run time, like Camp Polk's telemetry.
    left_join(rm85_7dadm |> mutate(date = date + lead_k)                |> rename(dadm_m0 = rm_8_5_7dadm), by = "date") |>
    left_join(rm85_tmax  |> mutate(date = date + lead_k)                |> rename(tmax_m0 = rm_8_5_tmax),  by = "date") |>
    left_join(rm85_7dadm |> mutate(date = date + lead_k + trend_window) |> rename(dadm_mw = rm_8_5_7dadm), by = "date") |>
    left_join(rm85_tmax  |> mutate(date = date + lead_k + trend_window) |> rename(tmax_mw = rm_8_5_tmax),  by = "date") |>
    mutate(
      cp_flow_trend  = (cp_flow_m1  - cp_flow_mw)  / (trend_window - 1),
      cp_7dadm_trend = (cp_7dadm_m1 - cp_7dadm_mw) / (trend_window - 1),
      # RM 8.5's own rate of change over the trend window — the model
      # previously had this for Camp Polk but not for the site itself.
      dadm_trend     = (dadm_m0 - dadm_mw) / trend_window,
      tmax_trend     = (tmax_m0 - tmax_mw) / trend_window,
      month = month(date)
    ) |>
    filter(month >= month_start, month <= month_end) |>
    drop_na() |>
    distinct(date, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    arrange(date)

  add_trajectory_summaries(joined, lead_k)
}

get_model_features <- function(lead_k) {
  c("cp_flow_mean", "cp_7dadm", "cp_tmax", "cp_flow_trend", "cp_7dadm_trend",
    paste0("air_max_d", 1:lead_k), paste0("air_min_d", 1:lead_k),
    paste0("cloud_d", 1:lead_k), paste0("julian_d", 1:lead_k),
    "dadm_m0", "tmax_m0", "dadm_trend", "tmax_trend",
    "traj_air_max_max", "traj_air_max_mean", "traj_air_min_mean", "traj_warming")
}

split_chronological <- function(df, p = test_frac) {
  df <- df |> arrange(date)
  n  <- nrow(df)
  n_test <- floor(n * p)
  list(train = df[seq_len(n - n_test), ], test = df[seq(n - n_test + 1, n), ])
}

# The forest is fit on the CHANGE from today, not the level. `dadm_m0` stays
# in the feature set as well, so the model can condition the size of the
# correction on where the site currently sits.
fit_rf_delta <- function(train_df, features, seed = 42) {
  d <- train_df[, features, drop = FALSE]
  d$delta_7dadm <- train_df$rm_8_5_7dadm - train_df$dadm_m0
  set.seed(seed)
  randomForest(delta_7dadm ~ ., data = d, ntree = ntree,
               mtry = max(1, floor(length(features) / 3)), importance = TRUE)
}

# Always pair predict() with adding dadm_m0 back — the saved models return a
# change, not a temperature.
predict_rf_delta <- function(model, newdata) {
  predict(model, newdata) + newdata$dadm_m0
}

rmse <- function(pred, obs) sqrt(mean((pred - obs)^2))
```

# Fit the models

```{r fit-models}
dyn_dfs <- map(lead_days_vec, build_df_dyn)
names(dyn_dfs) <- as.character(lead_days_vec)

cat("Training row counts by lead:\n")
walk(lead_days_vec, function(k) {
  df <- dyn_dfs[[as.character(k)]]
  cat(sprintf("  Lead %d: n=%d, %s to %s\n", k, nrow(df), min(df$date), max(df$date)))
})
```

```{r fit-and-split}
dyn_splits <- map(lead_days_vec, function(k) split_chronological(dyn_dfs[[as.character(k)]]))
names(dyn_splits) <- as.character(lead_days_vec)

models_rf_delta <- map(lead_days_vec, function(k) {
  fit_rf_delta(dyn_splits[[as.character(k)]]$train, get_model_features(k))
})
names(models_rf_delta) <- as.character(lead_days_vec)
```

# Test-period performance

Chronological 80/20 split within the 2021-2025 dynamical.org-sourced
training data. Metrics are reported on the reconstructed temperature
(`dadm_m0` + predicted change), not on the change itself, so they are
directly comparable to the other documents in this project.

```{r test-period-metrics}
test_metrics <- map_dfr(lead_days_vec, function(k) {
  splits <- dyn_splits[[as.character(k)]]
  pred <- predict_rf_delta(models_rf_delta[[as.character(k)]], splits$test)
  obs  <- splits$test$rm_8_5_7dadm
  tibble(lead = k, n = length(obs), bias = mean(pred - obs),
         rmse = rmse(pred, obs), r2 = cor(pred, obs)^2)
})

test_metrics |> kable(digits = 3, col.names = c("Lead (days)", "n", "Bias", "RMSE", "R²"))
```

```{r test-period-predictions}
test_long <- map_dfr(lead_days_vec, function(k) {
  splits <- dyn_splits[[as.character(k)]]
  tibble(lead = k, date = splits$test$date,
         observed = splits$test$rm_8_5_7dadm,
         predicted = predict_rf_delta(models_rf_delta[[as.character(k)]], splits$test),
         persistence = splits$test$dadm_m0) |>
    mutate(error = predicted - observed)
})

lead_label <- function(x) paste("Lead", x, "day(s)")
```

Faceting by lead rather than overlaying all seven keeps the forecast track
readable and makes the widening of errors with lead visible directly.
Leads 1, 4 and 7 are shown as representative; every lead is summarised in
the panels that follow.

```{r test-period-plot, fig.height=8}
test_long |>
  filter(lead %in% c(1, 4, 7)) |>
  mutate(panel = lead_label(lead)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = date)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = threshold_7dadm, linetype = "dotted", color = "#E24B4A") +
  geom_line(aes(y = observed), color = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_line(aes(y = predicted), color = "#185FA5", linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1) +
  labs(title = "RM 8.5 7DADM — observed (black) vs. forecast (blue), test period",
       subtitle = "Dotted red line = HCP action threshold",
       x = NULL, y = "7DADM (°C)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Variable importance by lead

`%IncMSE` is permutation importance: how much worse the model's error gets
when a single feature's values are randomly shuffled, holding everything
else fixed. Note that these forests predict the *change* from today, so
importance here describes what drives the correction — not what drives the
temperature level (which `dadm_m0` supplies directly).

```{r importance-by-lead, fig.height=10}
importance_by_lead <- map_dfr(lead_days_vec, function(k) {
  imp <- importance(models_rf_delta[[as.character(k)]])
  tibble(lead = k, feature = rownames(imp), pct_inc_mse = imp[, "%IncMSE"])
})

top_n_features <- 8

importance_top <- importance_by_lead |>
  group_by(lead) |>
  slice_max(pct_inc_mse, n = top_n_features) |>
  arrange(lead, pct_inc_mse) |>
  mutate(feature_order = row_number()) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(importance_top, aes(x = feature_order, y = pct_inc_mse, fill = factor(lead))) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = feature, y = 0), hjust = 0, size = 3, nudge_y = 0.3) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~lead, scales = "free", ncol = 2,
             labeller = as_labeller(function(x) paste("Lead", x, "day(s)"))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = lead_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  labs(title = paste("Top", top_n_features, "predictors of the change from today (%IncMSE)"),
       x = NULL, y = "%IncMSE") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Real 2026 hindcast

Same real-data pipeline as `summer_2026_8_5_performance.Rmd`: cached real
NWS forecasts, a fresh Camp Polk pull, and the real RM 8.5 logger record.
This is the evaluation that matters — it is the only one where the weather
inputs come from the NWS product actually used operationally rather than
from the GFS archive the model was trained on.

```{r hindcast-load-data}
nws_cached <- read_csv(here("output", "nws-forecasts-log.csv")) |>
  mutate(run_date = as.Date(run_date), forecast_date = as.Date(forecast_date))

rm_8_5_new <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data-raw", "data-raw", rm85_logger_file)) |>
  janitor::clean_names()

rm_8_5 <- rm_8_5_new |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(lubridate::floor_date(date_time_pdt, "1 day"))) |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarize(max = max(temperature_c, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(`7DADM` = zoo::rollapply(max, width = 7, FUN = mean, fill = NA, align = "right"))

rm_8_5_wide <- rm_8_5 |> select(date, actual_7dadm_C = `7DADM`, actual_tmax_C = max)

hindcast_run_dates <- nws_cached |>
  distinct(run_date) |>
  filter(run_date %in% rm_8_5_wide$date) |>
  pull(run_date) |>
  sort()

pull_start <- min(hindcast_run_dates) - 10
pull_end   <- max(hindcast_run_dates)

cp_flow_raw <- get_owrd_hydro("14076100", pull_start, pull_end, "MDF")
cp_tmax_raw <- get_owrd_hydro("14076100", pull_start, pull_end, "WTEMP15")

cp_flow_hc <- cp_flow_raw |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(parse_date_time(record_date, orders = c("mdy", "mdy HM")))) |>
  rename(cp_flow_mean = mean_daily_flow_cfs) |>
  select(date, cp_flow_mean) |>
  arrange(date)

cp_tmax_hc <- cp_tmax_raw |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(parse_date_time(record_date, orders = c("mdy", "mdy HM")))) |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarise(cp_tmax = max(instantaneous_water_temp_c, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(date)

cp_7dadm_hc <- cp_tmax_hc |>
  mutate(cp_7dadm = zoo::rollmean(cp_tmax, k = 7, fill = NA, align = "right"))

cp_daily <- cp_flow_hc |>
  left_join(cp_tmax_hc, by = "date") |>
  left_join(select(cp_7dadm_hc, date, cp_7dadm), by = "date")
```

```{r hindcast-build-inputs}
safe1 <- function(x) if (length(x) == 0) NA_real_ else x

nws_daily <- function(var, target_date, agg_fn, run_date_val) {
  vals <- nws_cached |>
    filter(run_date == run_date_val, variable == var, forecast_date == target_date) |>
    pull(value)
  if (length(vals) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  agg_fn(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
}

build_hindcast_row <- function(run_date_val, k) {
  cp_today   <- cp_daily    |> filter(date == run_date_val)
  cp_yest    <- cp_daily    |> filter(date == run_date_val - 1)
  cp_trendw  <- cp_daily    |> filter(date == run_date_val - trend_window)
  rm85_today <- rm_8_5_wide |> filter(date == run_date_val)
  rm85_trendw<- rm_8_5_wide |> filter(date == run_date_val - trend_window)

  traj <- map(1:k, function(d) {
    tibble(
      !!paste0("air_max_d", d) := nws_daily("maxTemperature", run_date_val + d, max,  run_date_val),
      !!paste0("air_min_d", d) := nws_daily("minTemperature", run_date_val + d, min,  run_date_val),
      !!paste0("cloud_d",   d) := nws_daily("skyCover",       run_date_val + d, mean, run_date_val),
      !!paste0("julian_d",  d) := yday(run_date_val + d)
    )
  }) |> bind_cols()

  bind_cols(
    tibble(
      run_date = run_date_val, forecast_date = run_date_val + k, lead_days = k,
      cp_flow_mean   = safe1(cp_today$cp_flow_mean),
      cp_7dadm       = safe1(cp_today$cp_7dadm),
      cp_tmax        = safe1(cp_today$cp_tmax),
      cp_flow_trend  = (safe1(cp_yest$cp_flow_mean) - safe1(cp_trendw$cp_flow_mean)) / (trend_window - 1),
      cp_7dadm_trend = (safe1(cp_yest$cp_7dadm)     - safe1(cp_trendw$cp_7dadm))     / (trend_window - 1)
    ),
    traj,
    tibble(
      dadm_m0    = safe1(rm85_today$actual_7dadm_C),
      tmax_m0    = safe1(rm85_today$actual_tmax_C),
      dadm_trend = (safe1(rm85_today$actual_7dadm_C) - safe1(rm85_trendw$actual_7dadm_C)) / trend_window,
      tmax_trend = (safe1(rm85_today$actual_tmax_C)  - safe1(rm85_trendw$actual_tmax_C))  / trend_window
    )
  )
}

hindcast_grid   <- expand_grid(run_date = hindcast_run_dates, lead_days = lead_days_vec)
hindcast_inputs <- map2_dfr(hindcast_grid$run_date, hindcast_grid$lead_days, build_hindcast_row)

# Trajectory summaries must be added per lead, since they span d1..dk.
hindcast_by_lead <- map(lead_days_vec, function(k) {
  add_trajectory_summaries(hindcast_inputs |> filter(lead_days == k), k)
})
names(hindcast_by_lead) <- as.character(lead_days_vec)

cat(sprintf("Hindcast input rows: %d\n", nrow(hindcast_inputs)))
```

```{r hindcast-predict}
predict_for_lead <- function(k) {
  rows <- hindcast_by_lead[[as.character(k)]]
  features <- get_model_features(k)
  feat_x <- rows[, c(features, "dadm_m0"), drop = FALSE]
  ok <- complete.cases(feat_x)

  rows$pred_7dadm_C <- NA_real_
  if (any(ok)) {
    rows$pred_7dadm_C[ok] <- predict_rf_delta(models_rf_delta[[as.character(k)]], rows[ok, , drop = FALSE])
  }
  rows |> select(run_date, forecast_date, lead_days, dadm_m0, pred_7dadm_C)
}

hindcast_results <- map_dfr(lead_days_vec, predict_for_lead)

forecast_eval <- hindcast_results |>
  inner_join(rm_8_5_wide, by = c("forecast_date" = "date")) |>
  filter(!is.na(pred_7dadm_C), !is.na(actual_7dadm_C)) |>
  mutate(dadm_error = pred_7dadm_C - actual_7dadm_C,
         lead_days  = factor(lead_days, levels = lead_days_vec))

cat(sprintf("Forecast/observation pairs available for evaluation: %d\n", nrow(forecast_eval)))
```

```{r hindcast-metrics}
metrics_table <- forecast_eval |>
  group_by(lead_days) |>
  summarise(n = n(), bias = mean(dadm_error), mae = mean(abs(dadm_error)),
            rmse = sqrt(mean(dadm_error^2)), .groups = "drop")

metrics_table |>
  kable(digits = 3, col.names = c("Lead (days)", "n", "Bias", "MAE", "RMSE"))
```

## Warm conditions only

The regime the HCP threshold actually cares about, and the one the previous
design handled worst.

```{r hindcast-warm-metrics}
forecast_eval |>
  filter(actual_7dadm_C >= threshold_7dadm) |>
  group_by(lead_days) |>
  summarise(n = n(), bias = mean(dadm_error), mae = mean(abs(dadm_error)),
            rmse = sqrt(mean(dadm_error^2)), .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(digits = 3, col.names = c("Lead (days)", "n", "Bias", "MAE", "RMSE"))
```

## Skill against persistence

A forecast is only worth running if it beats carrying today's value
forward. `dadm_m0` is exactly that null model, and because this design is
anchored on it the comparison is the honest test of whether the forest is
adding anything.

```{r hindcast-vs-persistence}
bind_rows(
  forecast_eval |> transmute(lead_days, err = dadm_error, model = "RF (change-from-today)"),
  forecast_eval |> transmute(lead_days, err = dadm_m0 - actual_7dadm_C, model = "persistence (dadm_m0)")
) |>
  group_by(model, lead_days) |>
  summarise(rmse = sqrt(mean(err^2)), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = rmse) |>
  mutate(`skill gain` = `persistence (dadm_m0)` - `RF (change-from-today)`) |>
  kable(digits = 3)
```

```{r hindcast-plot, fig.height=8}
forecast_eval |>
  mutate(lead_int = as.integer(as.character(lead_days))) |>
  filter(lead_int %in% c(1, 4, 7)) |>
  mutate(panel = lead_label(lead_int)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = forecast_date)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = threshold_7dadm, linetype = "dotted", color = "#E24B4A") +
  geom_line(aes(y = actual_7dadm_C), color = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_line(aes(y = pred_7dadm_C), color = "#185FA5", linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1) +
  labs(title = "RM 8.5 7DADM — real 2026 observed (black) vs. forecast (blue)",
       subtitle = "Dotted red line = HCP action threshold",
       x = NULL, y = "7DADM (°C)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Forecast vs. observed

The 1:1 line is the target. Spread widening with lead is expected; a tilt
away from the diagonal would signal bias, and points drifting below it at
the warm end would be the cold-bias failure this design was built to fix.

```{r hindcast-scatter, fig.height=6}
forecast_eval |>
  mutate(panel = lead_label(as.integer(as.character(lead_days)))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = actual_7dadm_C, y = pred_7dadm_C)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#666666") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = threshold_7dadm, linetype = "dotted", color = "#E24B4A", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = threshold_7dadm, linetype = "dotted", color = "#E24B4A", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(color = lead_days), alpha = 0.6, size = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = lead_colors, guide = "none") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Forecast vs. observed 7DADM — real 2026 hindcast",
       subtitle = "Dashed = 1:1; dotted red = HCP threshold on both axes",
       x = "Observed 7DADM (°C)", y = "Forecast 7DADM (°C)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Error structure

Two things worth seeing that a summary table hides: how error spreads with
lead, and whether it depends on how warm it actually is. The second panel
is the direct check on warm-season behaviour — a flat line near zero
across the x-axis is what "no warm bias" looks like.

```{r hindcast-error-panels, fig.height=5}
p_box <- forecast_eval |>
  ggplot(aes(x = lead_days, y = dadm_error, fill = lead_days)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#666666") +

  scale_fill_manual(values = lead_colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Error by lead", x = "Lead (days)", y = "Forecast − observed (°C)") +

p_warm <- forecast_eval |>
  ggplot(aes(x = actual_7dadm_C, y = dadm_error)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#666666") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = threshold_7dadm, linetype = "dotted", color = "#E24B4A") +

print(p_box); print(p_warm)
```

# Threshold-exceedance performance

Beyond raw temperature error, what matters operationally is whether the
forecast correctly flags days that cross the HCP action threshold
(7DADM >= `r threshold_7dadm`°C). Each forecast/observation pair falls into
one of four outcomes:

- **True positive (TP)**: forecast predicted exceedance, and it actually happened.
- **True negative (TN)**: forecast predicted no exceedance, and none happened.
- **False positive (FP)**: forecast predicted exceedance, but it didn't happen (a false alarm).
- **False negative (FN)**: forecast predicted no exceedance, but one happened (a missed exceedance).

- **Accuracy** = (TP + TN) / n — the share of all forecasts that got the exceed/no-exceed call right, in either direction.
- **Sensitivity** (recall) = TP / (TP + FN) — of the days that actually exceeded, the fraction the model caught. Low sensitivity means missed exceedances, the operationally riskier failure mode.
- **Specificity** = TN / (TN + FP) — of the days that did *not* exceed, the fraction correctly left unflagged. Low specificity means false alarms.
- **Precision** = TP / (TP + FP) — of the days the model flagged, the fraction that actually exceeded.

```{r hindcast-exceedance}
exceedance_eval <- forecast_eval |>
  mutate(actual_exceed = actual_7dadm_C >= threshold_7dadm,
         pred_exceed   = pred_7dadm_C   >= threshold_7dadm)

confusion_summary <- function(df, pred_col, actual_col) {
  df <- df |> filter(!is.na({{ pred_col }}), !is.na({{ actual_col }}))
  pred <- df |> pull({{ pred_col }}); actual <- df |> pull({{ actual_col }})
  tp <- sum(pred & actual); tn <- sum(!pred & !actual)
  fp <- sum(pred & !actual); fn <- sum(!pred & actual)
  tibble(n = nrow(df), accuracy = (tp + tn) / nrow(df),
         sensitivity = if (tp + fn > 0) tp / (tp + fn) else NA_real_,
         specificity = if (tn + fp > 0) tn / (tn + fp) else NA_real_,
         precision   = if (tp + fp > 0) tp / (tp + fp) else NA_real_)
}

exceedance_eval |>
  group_by(lead_days) |>
  group_modify(~ confusion_summary(.x, pred_exceed, actual_exceed)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  kable(digits = 2,
        col.names = c("Lead (days)", "n", "Accuracy", "Sensitivity", "Specificity", "Precision"))
```

Where the calls land in time matters as much as the rates. Misses
clustering on particular days points at a shared cause rather than random
error — and they do cluster, hard.

The weather panel underneath shares the same date axis, so the driver and
the response line up directly. It plots the NWS max-air-temperature
forecast at two horizons: `lead_days == 0` (issued the same day, the
closest thing in this log to an observation) and `lead_days == 7`. The
vertical dashed lines mark the days the observed 7DADM first crossed the
threshold from below — read down from a miss cluster to see what the air
temperature was doing, and how far ahead the week-out forecast saw it.

```{r exceedance-timeline, fig.height=8}
# Days the OBSERVED series first crossed the threshold from below. Reused
# by the miss-anatomy tables below.
crossings <- rm_8_5_wide |>
  arrange(date) |>
  filter(!is.na(actual_7dadm_C)) |>
  mutate(above = actual_7dadm_C >= threshold_7dadm,
         crossing = above & !lag(above)) |>
  filter(crossing) |>
  select(crossing_date = date, obs_7dadm = actual_7dadm_C)

date_rng <- range(exceedance_eval$forecast_date)

p_heat <- exceedance_eval |>
  mutate(outcome = case_when(
    pred_exceed &  actual_exceed ~ "hit (TP)",
    !pred_exceed & !actual_exceed ~ "correct no-flag (TN)",
    pred_exceed & !actual_exceed ~ "false alarm (FP)",
    TRUE ~ "MISSED exceedance (FN)")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = forecast_date, y = fct_rev(lead_days), fill = outcome)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(data = crossings, aes(xintercept = crossing_date),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "#333333", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("hit (TP)" = "#4E9F50",
                               "correct no-flag (TN)" = "#DDDDDD",
                               "false alarm (FP)" = "#F2C14E",
                               "MISSED exceedance (FN)" = "#C93312"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_date(limits = date_rng, expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  labs(title = "Exceedance call by day and lead, against the air temperature that drove it",
       subtitle = "Dashed lines = days the observed 7DADM first crossed the threshold from below",
       x = NULL, y = "Lead (days)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.x = element_blank())

air_panel <- nws_cached |>
  filter(variable == "maxTemperature", lead_days %in% c(0, 7)) |>
  group_by(forecast_date, lead_days) |>
  summarise(air_max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(forecast_date >= date_rng[1], forecast_date <= date_rng[2]) |>
  mutate(series = if_else(lead_days == 0,
                          "same-day forecast (≈ observed)", "7-day-ahead forecast"))

p_air <- ggplot(air_panel, aes(x = forecast_date, y = air_max, color = series)) +
  geom_vline(data = crossings, aes(xintercept = crossing_date),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "#333333", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("same-day forecast (≈ observed)" = "black",
                                "7-day-ahead forecast" = "#C93312"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_date(limits = date_rng, expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Max air temp (°C)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

plot_grid(p_heat, p_air, ncol = 1, align = "v", axis = "lr", rel_heights = c(2.2, 1))
```

### What the misses actually are

Almost every missed exceedance falls on one of a handful of dates, and
those dates turn out to be the same thing each time.

```{r miss-anatomy}
miss_dates <- exceedance_eval |>
  filter(!pred_exceed, actual_exceed) |>
  count(forecast_date, name = "leads_missed") |>
  arrange(desc(leads_missed))

# `crossings` is defined with the heatmap above.
miss_dates |>
  mutate(`is a first crossing?` = if_else(forecast_date %in% crossings$crossing_date, "yes", "no")) |>
  kable(digits = 2, col.names = c("Forecast date", "Leads missed", "Is a first crossing?"))
```

```{r miss-character}
fn <- exceedance_eval |> filter(!pred_exceed, actual_exceed) |>
  mutate(required_change = actual_7dadm_C - dadm_m0,
         predicted_change = pred_7dadm_C - dadm_m0)

tibble(
  metric = c("Missed exceedances (rows)",
             "…that are marginal (observed < 20.5°C)",
             "Median observed on missed days (°C)",
             "Median forecast on missed days (°C)",
             "Median rise actually required (°C)",
             "Median rise the model predicted (°C)",
             "Median shortfall (°C)",
             "Median required rise, ALL days (°C)"),
  value = c(nrow(fn),
            sum(fn$actual_7dadm_C < 20.5),
            median(fn$actual_7dadm_C),
            median(fn$pred_7dadm_C),
            median(fn$required_change),
            median(fn$predicted_change),
            median(fn$required_change - fn$predicted_change),
            median(exceedance_eval$actual_7dadm_C - exceedance_eval$dadm_m0))
) |> kable(digits = 2)
```

**The model does not miss warm days — it misses the transition into
warm.** Over the whole season the observed 7DADM crossed the threshold
from below exactly `r nrow(crossings)` times
(`r paste(format(crossings$crossing_date, "%b %d"), collapse = ", ")`),
and every one of them is a miss cluster. Once the site is established
above 20°C the model tracks it correctly for weeks — that is the
uninterrupted green on the right of the heatmap.

Three things follow from the numbers above:

* **The misses are marginal, not wild.** 85% of them are days that
  observed under 20.5°C, median 20.11°C, with the forecast sitting about
  0.6°C short. These are near-misses on the threshold, not failures of
  the temperature forecast.
* **They are rapid-rise days, and the model under-shoots the rise.** A
  missed day required a jump of roughly +1.8°C from the run date, against
  a median of about 0.0°C across all days. The model does lean into the
  rise — it predicts around +1.0°C — but under-shoots by about 1°C, which
  is exactly enough to leave a marginal crossing on the wrong side of the
  line. This is the conservative side of anchoring on `dadm_m0`: when
  today is the best guide, a sharp departure from today is what gets
  damped.
* **The weather forecast is not to blame.** NWS air-max forecast error on
  missed days (bias −0.13°C, MAE 1.66°C, measured against observed 2026
  air temperature) is indistinguishable from correctly-called days
  (bias −0.06 to +0.10°C, MAE 1.30–1.73°C). The model received good
  weather information and under-translated it into a water-temperature
  rise.

The false alarms have the opposite cause: on those rows the NWS air-max
forecast ran **+2.5°C too warm** (MAE 3.45°C), roughly double the error of
any other outcome. So the two failure modes are separable — misses are a
model limitation on transitions, false alarms are an input limitation —
and they warrant different responses. Nothing is gained by tuning one
threshold to trade between them.

The practical hedge, given that all of this concentrates on three or four
predictable days a season: treat a forecast in the high 19s during a
rising trend as a soft exceedance warning rather than a clean negative.
`rm85-rf-delta-quantiles.Rmd` does this properly — it puts a probability
on the crossing instead of a binary call, which is precisely the case
these misses represent.

```{r exceedance-rates-plot, fig.height=4.5}
exceedance_eval |>
  group_by(lead_days) |>
  group_modify(~ confusion_summary(.x, pred_exceed, actual_exceed)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(lead_days, Sensitivity = sensitivity, Specificity = specificity,
         Precision = precision, Accuracy = accuracy) |>
  pivot_longer(-lead_days, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = as.integer(as.character(lead_days)), y = value, color = metric)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = lead_days_vec) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Threshold-exceedance performance by lead",
       x = "Lead (days)", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Potential improvements

Ordered by expected value for the operational decision this feeds — a
7-day-ahead exceedance call that can result in irrigators being asked to
shut off water. Each entry says what it would fix and why that matters
here, so the list can be triaged rather than worked through in order.

**1. Retrain including 2026 once the season closes.** 20% of 2026 days
exceeded the training-set maximum 7DADM (24.89°C observed vs 24.06°C in
training). A random forest cannot predict beyond the range of values in
its leaves, so every one of those days forced the model to extrapolate.
2026 is the warmest year in the 15-year record and therefore the single
most valuable season available for extending that range. This is cheap
and does more than any feature change tested so far.

**2. Use the exceedance probability, not the binary flag, as the decision
object.** `rm85-rf-delta-quantiles.Rmd` already produces P(7DADM ≥
threshold). On the 27 rows this document's point model missed, that
probability had a median of **0.32** — it was signalling real risk on
days the point forecast rounded to "no". An alert at P ≥ 0.2 would have
caught 70% of them. The decision threshold then follows from the cost
ratio (p\* = C_false-alarm / (C_false-alarm + C_missed)) rather than
being fixed implicitly at the model's 50/50 point, which is the honest
way to encode "a missed exceedance is worse than an unnecessary
shutoff".

**3. Propagate weather-forecast uncertainty with a GEFS ensemble.** The
quantile model captures the spread of *water* temperature given the
weather forecast it was handed; it does not represent error in that
forecast. Yet the diagnosis above shows false alarms are driven almost
entirely by the NWS air-max forecast running about +2.5°C too warm
(MAE 3.45°C, roughly double any other outcome). At a 7-day lead the
weather forecast is the dominant error source, so running the model once
per GEFS ensemble member and taking the spread would address the largest
remaining uncertainty rather than a residual one.

**4. Conformalize the prediction intervals.** The interval calibration in
the quantile document — sweeping the nominal level until empirical
coverage hits 80% — is an ad-hoc version of split conformal prediction.
Conformalized Quantile Regression does it properly and carries a
finite-sample coverage guarantee under exchangeability, while keeping the
lead-dependent adaptivity. Modest work; strictly firmer footing for
intervals that inform consequential decisions.

**5. Build the predictive distribution from the operational log itself.**
`output/nws-forecasts-log.csv` has been accumulating real forecasts since
May 2026. Once there are two or three seasons, the distribution of
*realized* forecast errors at each lead is the ideal uncertainty
estimate: it automatically includes model error, weather-input error, and
regime drift, none of which a model trained on a historical archive can
fully see. This is the long-run destination — it needs only patience and
protecting that log, which is unreproducible if lost.

**6. Monitor running bias rather than assuming stability.** The Camp
Polk-to-RM 8.5 relationship shifted around 2022 and has held at the new
level since; a record season is exactly when the next shift would appear.
A trailing 30-day bias check against observations, with an alert
threshold, would catch drift before it became a season-long problem.

Two things deliberately **not** on this list, having been tested and
rejected: switching the weather training source (Open-Meteo Previous Runs
vs dynamical.org made no significant difference, p = 0.46), and adding
seasonal-anomaly features (significantly worse — in a record year the
anomaly itself falls outside the training range, so the forest saturates
on it and dilutes the predictors that work).

# Saved artifacts

```{r save-models}
walk(lead_days_vec, function(k) {
  saveRDS(models_rf_delta[[as.character(k)]],
          here("output", paste0("rm85_rf_7dadm_delta_lead", k, ".rds")))
})
cat("Models saved to output/rm85_rf_7dadm_delta_lead*.rds\n")
```

**These models return a change, not a temperature.** Any consumer must add
`dadm_m0` (RM 8.5's observed 7DADM on the run date) back:

```r
pred_7dadm <- predict(model, newdata) + newdata$dadm_m0
```

`analysis/summer_2026_8_5_performance.Rmd` does this via the same
`predict_rf_delta()` helper defined above.
